message.text:
No per-user API rate-limiting middleware exists in this repository.

The server registers middleware.Recover(), CORS, and gatewayAuthMiddleware. Semaphores limit concurrent image and thumbnail processing. Rate limiting is recommended in the email README but not implemented for API requests.

r02.

**Premise correction:** This repository does not implement per-user API rate-limiting middleware, and there is no registration site or request limit to report.

A repo-wide search finds no rate-limiting middleware (no `RateLimit`, `ratelimit`, or similar in server code). Echo middleware registered at startup is limited to recovery and CORS in `server/server.go:51-52`, plus static/SPA middleware in `server/router/frontend/frontend.go`. The API layer uses auth middleware/interceptors (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69`, `server/router/api/v1/authz.go`), not rate limiting.

The closest limits are unrelated to per-user API throughput:
- Concurrent semaphores for thumbnail/image processing (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`: 3 and 2 concurrent operations)
- Pagination/content-length limits in individual handlers
- Email rate limiting mentioned only as documentation guidance in `internal/email/README.md`, not as API middleware

So the question’s premise does not match the codebase: there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware here.
